label: Wilmington to Philadelphia (Thomas Garrett)
source: Foner, "Middle Atlantic", NPS Underground Railroad Handbook (Dickinson, HB-FONER); Wikipedia, "Thomas Garrett" (WP-GARRETT)

Garrett worked in Wilmington from 1822 and sent people on to the Philadelphia committee. 1861: J. Miller McKim's remark that the Underground Railroad was in effect over (HB-FONER); the NPS itself runs it to 1865. Places, in order: Wilmington, Philadelphia.

label: Eastern Shore of Maryland to Wilmington (Harriet Tubman's route)
source: NPS, Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad NHP, "Harriet Tubman" (NPS-TUB); Wikipedia, "Harriet Tubman", citing Larson 2004 and Clinton 2004 (WP-TUB)
qc_note: TEST ROW for the Underground Railroad layer (owner's request of 2026-11-17); not reviewed. Research and full citations: docs/UNDERGROUND-RAILROAD.md. Poplar Neck near Preston, then Sandtown, Camden (the Brinkleys and Abraham Gibbs), past Dover and Smyrna, New Castle, Wilmington (Garrett), Philadelphia (William Still). Her own escape, autumn 1849; return trips 1850 to 1860. This is the chain of her later trips as Larson reconstructs it: the way of her first escape is not known. East New Market (Sam Green) and Willow Grove are on the chain in the source and left off the line, which is too short to show them apart. Places, in order: Preston, Sandtown, Camden, Dover, Smyrna, New Castle, Wilmington, Philadelphia.

label: Philadelphia to New York
source: Foner, "Middle Atlantic" (HB-FONER); NPS handbook timeline (HB-TIME)
qc_note: TEST ROW for the Underground Railroad layer (owner's request of 2026-11-17); not reviewed. Research and full citations: docs/UNDERGROUND-RAILROAD.md. 1835: David Ruggles founds the New York Committee of Vigilance. By train and ferry across New Jersey; no source read names a New Jersey town except Siebert (1898), from recollections. Places, in order: Philadelphia, New York.

label: New York to Canada by Albany, Syracuse and Niagara

Albany (Stephen Myers), Syracuse (Jermain Loguen), Rochester (Frederick Douglass), Buffalo, the Niagara crossing, St. Catharines. 1842: Charles Torrey's party reaches Albany, the earliest dated use of the road north of New York in what was read; Sydney Howard Gay's record of 1855 to 1856 documents Syracuse best. The Albany leg is less fully attested than the Syracuse leg. Places, in order: New York, Albany, Syracuse, Rochester, Buffalo, Niagara Falls, St. Catharines.

One documented journey; many who reached New England stayed there. Places, in order: New York, Hartford, Springfield.

label: Albany to Canada through Vermont
source: Siebert, The Underground Railroad from Slavery to Freedom (1898), ch. V (SIEBERT-V); Grover (HB-GROVER)
qc_note: TEST ROW for the Underground Railroad layer (owner's request of 2026-11-17); not reviewed. Research and full citations: docs/UNDERGROUND-RAILROAD.md. Robinson, 1838), Burlington (Joshua Young) and St. Albans (people forwarded by train, 1854 and 1856), and warns that Vermont was less safe than tradition says. Places, in order: Albany, Troy, Bennington, Rutland, Ferrisburgh, Burlington, St. Albans, Montreal.

The ports are documented; the line at sea is schematic, run by Cape Henry and Cape Henlopen to keep it off the land. Places, in order: Norfolk, Cape Henry, Cape Henlopen, Wilmington, Philadelphia.

Places, in order: Philadelphia, Harrisburg, Williamsport, Elmira, Watkins Glen, Canandaigua, Rochester.

label: Louisiana to Mexican Texas

Natchitoches as the line's start is the editor's choice (WP-UGRR mentions a road from there); the escapes the source dates were from parishes farther south. Ends in 1836, when Texas left Mexico. Places, in order: Natchitoches, Nacogdoches, San Antonio.
